paras: Good evening, Mr. de Souza. Here is Thursday, so you have it before you sleep.
MORNING. The car is at the hotel door at seven thirty in the morning, not at eight. Breakfast is from seven, so you have half an hour. The driver's name is Paul.
The first meeting is at nine, in the old building on Market Street. It is from nine to eleven. After that you are free until lunch.
AFTERNOON. Lunch is at one, and it is a long one, maybe two hours. In the afternoon there is nothing until five. At five thirty there is a short visit, twenty minutes, ten minutes from the hotel.
EVENING. Dinner is at eight, at the Blue Door, and we are nine people. Please be early, because the restaurant is small and they close the kitchen at ten thirty.
One change from yesterday: the meeting on Friday is now in the morning, not in the afternoon. Friday morning, at ten.

listenings.text: Hi, this is Paul, your driver. This message is about tomorrow. There are two changes. First, the car is at the hotel at seven thirty in the morning, not at eight. The traffic on Thursday is very bad after eight. So, seven thirty, not eight. Second, in the afternoon I am not free at five. I have another car at that time. At five, your driver is my colleague. His name is Tomas. Same car, different driver. Dinner is the same, at eight in the evening, and after dinner I am your driver back to the hotel. Is seven thirty too early for you? Please call me tonight, not tomorrow morning. Thank you, and good night.

Here is my day. It is not difficult. I get up at five thirty, every day. From six to seven I walk. That is my hour, only for me. I have breakfast at seven with my children. I start work at eight thirty, and I stop at six. I do not answer the phone after eight in the evening. On Saturday I work in the morning, but never in the afternoon. On Sunday I do nothing. That is not lazy. It is the reason the other six days are good. I go to bed at ten. That is all. No secret.

extra_audio.text: Good morning. What time is the car tomorrow? At seven thirty, not at eight? And the meeting is at nine. Is that right? I finish at eleven. See you in the morning.
